title: The Sneaky-Prover Detection Gap Across Model Families

original_idea.body:
# The Sneaky-Prover Detection Gap Across Model Families

**Problem:** It is unknown how well a verifier from one model family detects sneaky solutions produced by an unrelated family.

**Direction:** Generate sneaky-wrong and helpful-correct math/reasoning solutions from several open model families and cross-evaluate: each family's model acts as verifier on every other family's outputs. Build a detection-accuracy matrix and look for blind spots.

**Why it matters:** Real oversight pairs models from different lineages; shared blind spots are a hidden single point of failure.

**Relevant context:** Kirchner et al. (2024, arXiv:2407.13692); arXiv:2510.11235.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: cross-family blind spots are a concrete single-point-of-failure for model-overseeing-model setups.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Generate + cross-evaluate solutions across families is guided; building the matrix is mechanical.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused detection-matrix deliverable; multiple families add some bookkeeping dependency.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Correlated-failure/cross-family scrutiny is external-friendly gold, no internal access.

novelty.reasoning: Sneaky-prover framing exists; the cross-family detection matrix may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: PVG exists; cross-family blind-spot matrix plausibly untested.
